title: 1. Meaning and Structure of State Legislature (Article 168)

blocks.content:
According to Article 168, the Legislature of a State consists of:
• Governor
• Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha)
• Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) – in some states

States may have either a unicameral or bicameral legislature.

rows: Governor + Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha) + Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad)

items: Note that the Governor is an integral component of the State Legislature under Article 168.
Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) is not mandatory for all states, leading to unicameral setups in many states.
Questions frequently test which article defines the structure of the State Legislature (Article 168).

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 168 governs the constitution and meaning of the State Legislature.
The State Legislature consists of the Governor, the Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha), and in some states, the Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad).
States are categorized as having either a unicameral or a bicameral legislative structure depending on the presence of the Legislative Council.
